title: GAO report: AI can magnify cyberattacks and also enhance cyber defense
summary: GAO's report GAO-27-108458, published 20 November 2026, says AI can magnify the reach and impact of traditional cyberattacks, including phishing and deepfake content, and that agentic AI carrying out multiple attack stages is an emerging trend. It says there are no widely accepted evaluation criteria for assessing offensive or defensive capabilities of generative AI. It presents four policy goals and 16 policy options.
plain: A US government watchdog report says AI can make cyberattacks bigger and faster, and can also help defenders. It lists options for policymakers.
exec: GAO says AI raises the reach of attacks such as phishing and deepfakes, and lists 16 policy options for government.

validation.note: GAO's own product page (highlights and policy-goal tables) and CASRAI's summary read; the 70-page PDF text could not be extracted.

review.note: Compared report number, 20 Nov date, magnify/phishing/deepfake and agentic wording, no-evaluation-criteria sentence, 4 goals/16 options against GAO product page and CASRAI; all match

key_findings: AI lets threat actors magnify traditional attacks, making phishing and deepfake content higher quality and attacks more precise and faster; agentic AI carrying out several attack stages is an emerging trend.

GAO's page cites a June 2026 case of a threat actor using multiple AI agents to test malware against security products, and a February 2026 reported case of a low-skill actor using commercial generative AI to exploit stolen passwords on devices with weak passwords and no multi-factor authentication.
Defenders use machine learning and generative AI for tasks such as vulnerability scanning, finding flaws in source code and parsing large volumes of network data.
There are no widely accepted criteria for judging offensive or defensive AI capability, and generative AI adds new risks that expand the attack surface.
GAO sets out four policy goals and 16 policy options (guidance gaps, research gaps, governing AI tools through their lifecycle, workforce), presented as a menu rather than an exhaustive list.
recommendations: No formal recommendations were seen on GAO's report page; the 70-page PDF text was not read.
